paper.title: A Latent Source Model for Online Collaborative Filtering

settings.name_in_paper: Latent source model for online recommendation (no repeat consumption)
unmapped: n users each recommended one item per step; m items (arms); each item can be recommended to a given user at most once
k latent user types, each user's type uniform over k; users of same type share preference vector p_u in [0,1]^m; ratings +1/-1 Bernoulli(p_ui)
objective: expected number of likable items (p_ui > 1/2) recommended, compared with an oracle recommending all likable items first
A1: |p_ui - 1/2| >= Delta for all u,i (no Delta-ambiguous items); A2: gamma-incoherence between types
algorithm needs Delta and gamma to set threshold theta = 2 Delta^2 (1+gamma); does not need k
settings.definition_quote: We consider a system with $n$ users and $m$ items. At each time step, each user is recommended an item that she or he hasn't consumed yet, upon which ... the user immediately consumes the item and rates it $+1$ (like) or $-1$ (dislike). ... we aim to maximize the expected number of \emph{likable} items recommended up to time $T$: r_+^{(T)} = \sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{u=1}^n \E[X_{ut}]

symbols.mu: minimum proportion of likable items for any user

conditions: A1: |p_ui - 1/2| >= Delta for all users and items
n = O(m^C) for some constant C > 1
each user's type uniform over k types

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Let $\delta\in(0,1)$ be some pre-specified tolerance. Take as input to \textsc{Collaborative-Greedy} $\theta = 2 \Delta^2 (1 + \gamma)$ ... if the number of users $n=O(m^C)$ satisfies $n = \Omega(km \log \frac{1}{\delta} + (\frac{4}{\delta})^{1/\alpha})$, then for any $\tc \le T \le \mu m$, the expected proportion of likable items recommended by \textsc{Collaborative-Greedy} up until time $T$ satisfies $\frac{r_+^{(T)}}{T n} \ge (1 - \frac{\tc}{T})(1-\delta)$

results.notes: This is a LOWER bound on the expected fraction of likable items recommended (a reward guarantee), not a regret bound; recorded with quantity 'other'. Implies a regret against the oracle of at most n*(T_learn + delta*T) but the paper does not state it that way. T_learn is given only up to Theta.

bound.regime: max{(2 log(10 k m n^alpha/Delta)/(Delta^4(1-gamma)^2))^(1/(1-alpha)), (20 log(96/delta)/(Delta^4(1-gamma)^2))^(1/(1-alpha)), (4/delta)^(1/alpha)} <= t <= mu*m

symbols.X_ut: indicator that the item recommended to user u at time t is likable

conditions: n t^(1-alpha) >= (40 k m/Delta^2) log(16 m/delta)

source.label: lem:general-conditions
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$ be some pre-specified tolerance. If the number of users $n$ and items $m$ satisfy ... then $\P(X_{ut}=1) \ge 1 - \delta.$

results.notes: Per-round probability that a likable item is recommended; a lower bound on success probability, recorded as 'other'.
